critical_code_review_comments: captions._create_browser_preview uses libvpx-vp9 -deadline realtime -cpu-used 8 -b:v 1100k + libopus -b:a 96k, which is the correct universal-browser combo (Chromium/Firefox/Safari-16+ all support VP9+Opus in WebM). On failure it logs and returns None; the caller then just proceeds without a preview_path and /media falls back to the source MP4 - acceptable graceful degradation. Consider recording preview_error on the project so the UI can surface 'preview unavailable, using source' rather than silently trying an incompatible MP4.

captions.project_media loads the entire file into RAM (get_object returns bytes) and slices it for every 206 response. For a 7.2 MB preview this is fine, but for a 120 MB source (allowed max) plus concurrent seeks it multiplies memory pressure. Consider streaming from object storage with a byte-range fetch, or caching the last-loaded file per project_id in memory. Not urgent given the WebM preview is small.

captions._run_caption_job kicks off preview_task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(_create_browser_preview, source, preview)) and only awaits it AFTER the (slower) transcription + hinglish steps complete. Good use of parallelism - preview is essentially free on the wall clock. But if transcription fails and raises before `preview_bytes = await preview_task`, the preview task keeps a temp directory file handle open via the enclosing `with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` context, which is torn down inside the except; the ffmpeg subprocess would likely just fail writing to the deleted path. Consider awaiting or cancelling preview_task in the except branch to avoid an orphaned ffmpeg.

captions.retranscribe_project now correctly clears words=[] and source_transcript='' when queuing Re-listen (addresses iter4 MEDIUM). No preview_path is cleared, so if a user re-listens on a project whose preview_path already exists, /media will keep serving the old WebM (matching the old audio) while the words update. This is a minor UX seam but not a correctness bug because a Re-listen changes only transcription, not the video content.

captions.project_media returns Response(chunk, ...) for 206 - the entire chunk is buffered in memory before send. Fine for <8 MB responses; if a client asks for bytes=0- on a 120 MB source the whole thing gets buffered. StreamingResponse with an iterator would be more forgiving.

rca of the issue: Iter4 fixed the /media endpoint to emit 206 for bounded Range but incorrectly capped open-ended bytes=0- to the first ~1 MB, and Chromium's H.264/AAC support in the Playwright build is absent so even a Range-compliant MP4 could not play. Iter5 audit confirms both defects are fully addressed: (1) Range handler now parses `bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)$` and treats an empty end as total-1 (see captions.py L347-356), so bytes=0- returns the full 7205644-byte body inside a single 206 with Content-Range: bytes 0-7205643/7205644 - verified by curl and by pytest TestOpenEndedRange::test_bytes_0_dash_is_honored_to_eof. (2) _run_caption_job now transcodes source MP4 -> 720-wide VP9/Opus WebM in parallel with Whisper via `asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(_create_browser_preview, ...))`, uploads to $APP_NAME/previews/{user_id}/*.webm, and stores preview_path + preview_content_type='video/webm' on the project before status=ready; project_media then prefers preview_path over source_path. This lets HTML5 <video> in Chromium play the file natively - verified: readyState=4, duration=37.695, seek to 20 advances to 22.44 during a 2.5s play, error=None. Also verified retranscribe_project now clears words=[] and source_transcript='' at queue time to eliminate the stale-word UX seam. No other functional changes needed.
